newsitem.title: USA: IMF's Camdessus praises Venezuela economic results.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus praises Venezuela economic results.

text.p: International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus praised Thursday the initial results of Venezuela's stabilization program.
"This is indeed a success story and I am confident that it will be a long lasting one," Camdessus said in the closing news conference of the IMF/World Bank annual meeting.
"The financial results of the program are so spectacular that Venezuela will not need to draw on what would normally be our contribution to the financing," he added.
Venezuelan Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar had said Wednesday his country would not require the disbursement of the second tranche of a $1.4 billion IMF stand-by loan.
According to Matos, Venezuela's foreign reserves had risen so rapidly to over $12 billion from around $10 billion earlier this year it would not need the IMF's money.
Camdessus praised Venezuela for undertaking reforms which it had previously viewed as politically impossible, such as cutting long-standing subsidies on gasoline prices.
"When one sees where we were one year ago and when one sees the sleeping giant of Venezuela walking again ... one can really be satisfied," he said.
